title: Market Body Labor Rates on Insurer Program Agreements
content:
Whether an insurer's agreement under the Insurer Program Agreements may carry a market-specific body labor rate in place of the tier's body labor rate, and how far apart two changes of that market rate must lie, is fixed per tier by two terms:

- **Market rate permitted** — whether a market-specific body labor rate may be set on the agreement in place of the tier rate (yes or no).
- **Market rate review interval** — the fewest calendar months between two changes of a market body labor rate on the agreement (a whole number of months; 0 means no override).

| Agreement tier | Market rate permitted | Market rate review interval (calendar months) |
|---|---|---|
| Network Referral Agreement | No | 0 |
| Select Direct Repair Agreement | Yes | 12 |
| Preferred Direct Repair Agreement | Yes | 12 |
| Premier Direct Repair Agreement | Yes | 12 |
| Managed Repair Program Agreement | Yes | 12 |
| Enterprise Master Services Agreement | Yes | 12 |

## Points of judgement

- Under a Network Referral Agreement no market body labor rate may be set, and its review interval reads 0, which the term itself defines as no override.
- Under every other tier a market body labor rate may be set, and two changes of it lie at least 12 calendar months apart.
- The interval is counted in calendar months between two changes of the market rate on the same agreement.

## Illustration (hypothetical dates)

On a hypothetical Preferred Direct Repair Agreement whose market body labor rate was last changed in March of one year, the fewest calendar months before the next change is 12, so the next change falls no earlier than March of the following year.
